summary.text: Alfred "Al" Taylor is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election in Assembly District 71, running unopposed. A pastor and former Assembly chief of staff, he has represented the district, covering Harlem, Washington Heights and Inwood, since winning a November 2017 special election. He serves on the Banks, Codes, Education, Election Law, Labor and Rules committees.

paragraphs.text: In a 2020 interview, Taylor said he serves and lives in the same district he grew up in, and described himself as a former military police officer.
He earned a B.A. in Public Communication from Lehman College, a Master of Divinity from Nyack College Alliance Theological Seminary, and a Doctorate of Ministry from Northeastern Seminary.

Before his election, Taylor served as Chief of Staff to former Assemblyman Herman "Denny" Farrell Jr. and as a Democratic district leader, and the Assembly biography cites more than 20 years of advocacy experience; in the 2020 interview he said he had worked for 27 years for the legislator he replaced.

In 2008 Taylor founded the "Man Up! in Harlem" anti-gun-violence program, organizing weekly prayer walks at Rucker Park; according to his Assembly biography the model was later replicated in other Upper Manhattan housing projects.
He is the pastor of Infinity Mennonite Church in Harlem; in 2020 he said he was in his 12th year of pastoring there and is not a salaried pastor.

Taylor won the November 7, 2017 special election, unopposed, for the seat vacated when Herman Farrell resigned on September 5, 2017, and took office that fall; he was re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024.
He is a member of the Black Task Force and the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus.

According to his Assembly biography, legislation he introduced and supported that became law includes a requirement that childcare services adopt anaphylaxis policies, creation of the Law Enforcement Misconduct Investigative Office, and the "Make Voting Easy Act" on early voting polling places.
The biography also says he walked 780 miles to Chicago in the "It's A Love Thing Always" event, and that he is married to Gwendolyn, has five children and lives in Northern Manhattan.

sources.title: Pastor & politician: In Capitol and pulpit, Al Taylor takes two paths to one mission (Anabaptist World, Oct. 28, 2020)
